The first arrow punched into the dirt beside her knee. The second snapped past her ear so close it felt like a whip of cold air. Kira flinched into the motion instead of away from it, twisting behind a broken shelf of stone with her breath already burning.

“Come on!” she snarled, slapping the flat of one blade against the rock. “That all you’ve got?”

Her eyes flicked upward. The two archers near the split boulder had leaned too far in their eagerness. One had his knee braced on the lip of the ridge. The other was trying to nock fast, bow angled down, silhouette sharp against the pale sky.

The southern pair were worse.

They had stopped trying to pin her and were edging along the ridge with their bows half-drawn, heads turning toward the western side of the ravine. Watching. Waiting for a clean line. If they settled behind that cut, they would have time to choose their shots.

Kira’s jaw tightened.

“South pair’s still loose!” she called toward the far side, voice raw. “They’ll loose the second anything stays still!”

No one answered that she could hear. Maybe the ravine stole it. Maybe there was no breath to spare.

She cursed under her breath and snatched up another stone. This one was bigger, rough-edged, awkward in her grip. She hurled it not at the archers but at a slab farther along the ridge. It struck with a loud, hollow crack and bounced away, echoing twice.

At the same time, she broke from cover.

The trick worked again, but only half. One archer jerked toward the sound and loosed too soon. The arrow whipped into the ravine wall and shattered. The other held his draw, searching.

Kira did not give him time.

She kicked a loose plate of shale hard enough to send it skittering down the slope, then raked her dagger across the stone beside it. More sparks. More noise. More movement.

“Over here!” she shouted. “Look at me, you blind shits!”

The searching archer found her.

His bow came around. Kira threw herself sideways as the string snapped. The arrow grazed the outside of her upper arm, not biting deep, but tearing cloth and dragging a hot line of pain across her skin.

“Fuck!” The word burst out before she could stop it.

She hit the ground hard, rolled, and came up behind the narrow spur again with her heart slamming against her ribs. Her arm stung. Her sleeve was torn. Blood welled, thin and bright, more insult than wound.

Still, she was alive. Still moving. Still the nearest thing on the east side worth shooting at.

Kira wiped her hand down her thigh and forced her breathing into some kind of order.

Above her, the ridge was shifting again. The two near the split boulder were creeping south to join the others. Four bows now, maybe five if one stayed low. They were getting bolder because they thought she was pinned. They thought she had run out of tricks.

She bared her teeth.

“Not yet,” she muttered.

Her eyes swept the ground around her. Loose stones. A dead scrub with roots like twisted fingers. A shallow crack in the cliff face, barely wide enough for a body. Not a route up. Not really. But it might look like one to a man who was already nervous.

Kira took one dagger in her teeth and jammed the other into the crack. Steel bit stone. She hauled herself up a few feet, boots scrabbling, making herself climb in plain sight.

The response was instant.

Two arrows snapped toward her. One struck the rock where her hip had been. The other buried itself in the bank near her hand, close enough that the shaft quivered.

Kira dropped back down, cursing around the dagger in her mouth, and landed in a crouch.

“Good,” she breathed. “Stay stupid.”

She could not see everything happening on the western side. She could hear it: the clash of metal, boots slipping on scree, voices strained and ragged. The fight had stretched too far. The vanguard was scattered, and the high ground was still trying to bleed it dry.

She could not fix that.

She could only make sure the east ridge did not get calm.

Kira snatched two more stones, then rose just enough to throw them. The first struck the split boulder with a sharp crack. The second hit the ledge beyond it and sent a shower of pebbles bouncing down. She followed the noise by raking both daggers across the stone in crossed, shrieking strokes, sparks flying in wild little arcs.

“Here!” she shouted. “Still here, you useless bastards!”

The southern pair hesitated. One turned back toward her. The other crouched lower, trying to find a line around the cut without exposing himself.

That hesitation was worth something.

Kira pressed her back against the spur and gripped her daggers tighter. Her arm throbbed. Grit clung to her sweat. Her pulse was loud in her ears, but her hands stayed steady.

“South pair’s split!” she called out, because even a small advantage was worth shouting. “One’s watching me, one’s still hunting west! Don’t let him settle behind the cut!”

Another arrow thudded into the rock above her. Stone chips rained down into her hair.

Kira did not duck this time. She laughed instead, short and ugly.

“Is that all?” she roared up at the ridge. “Come down and do it with steel, then!”

No one took the offer.

Good.

She shifted her weight, ready to sprint again, ready to throw more stones, make more noise, bleed more attention away from the western side. She could not cross the ravine. She could not put steel into the archers who mattered most. But she could keep the east ridge honest, one stupid trick at a time.

And if that meant every bow on her side of the killzone spent its arrows chasing a swearing, spark-throwing sellsword instead of settling into clean shots, then she would be the loudest damn fool in the ravine until the fight broke one way or the other.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *Kira's call about the south pair gives me an idea.* "Vanguard, form a wedge! Drive for that cut!" I order, pointing with my polearm. If we can punch through, we can get to those archers.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira caught the order through the ravine’s broken echoes, the words hammered thin by stone and distance but clear enough.

Wedge. Drive for the cut.

“About damn time,” she muttered, though there was no relief in it. Only the hard, narrow focus of someone who had just been given a reason to keep bleeding.

If the west side was going to punch for that cut, then the archers above her would have to make a choice: keep chasing the noisy bastard below the east ridge, or turn their bows toward the real threat. Kira intended to make the first choice look better.

She shoved away from the spur and moved fast along the base of the cliff, boots grinding over shattered stone. Her torn sleeve clung damply to her arm. The graze there still burned, a hot, irritated line that got worse every time she moved. She ignored it. Pain was information. Right now the information said she was still alive.

She snatched another rock from the ground, then another, jamming one into the crook of her elbow and gripping the second tight. The dead scrub nearby had roots like old knuckles. She kicked it hard, snapping dry wood, then dragged one dagger through the dirt and stone beside it. The scrape screamed up the ravine wall. Sparks jumped, brief and orange.

“Over here!” she shouted. “Still me, you useless shits!”

The east ridge answered.

An arrow punched into the slope a stride to her left. Another cracked against the cliff face higher up, sending chips raining down. Kira flinched into the motion instead of away from it, shoulders hunched, body low. She threw the first stone hard at a ledge beneath the split boulder. It struck with a sharp crack and bounced away, echoing louder than it had any right to. Then she threw the second wider, toward the southern end of the ridge.

Two bows snapped at the movement.

One shaft went high. The other hissed past her thigh close enough to tug at her trousers. Kira cursed and slid behind a slab so fast her knees nearly buckled.

“Still got arrows?” she called, breathing hard. “Good. Waste them on me.”

She risked a glance upward.

The archers near the split boulder were leaning too far again. One had braced his knee on the lip of the ridge. The other was nocking with quick, angry movements. Farther south, the pair she had been tracking were reacting to the shift below. One of them had turned his body away from her, attention dragging toward the western side of the ravine. The other remained half-crouched, bow ready, still trying to keep her in view.

That was the danger.

If the wedge drove hard for the cut, the southern archers would either panic and expose themselves or settle into a clean line and start picking targets. Kira had seen enough ambushes to know which one was more likely once the first man fell.

“South pair’s splitting!” she shouted toward the far side, voice raw from dust and yelling. “One’s turning to you! Keep moving or he’ll settle!”

She did not wait to hear if anyone answered. The ravine ate sound and gave back confusion. All she could do was make herself louder than the fight.

Kira jammed one dagger into a crack in the cliff face again and hauled herself up a few feet, boots scrabbling on loose stone. The movement was stupid, obvious, and exactly what the ridge wanted to see. A target climbing. A target trying to get up.

Two bows turned toward her at once.

“Ah, fuck,” she hissed, and dropped.

Arrows struck the rock where she had just been. One buried itself in the dirt bank with a dull thud. The other snapped off a splinter of stone near her shoulder, sending grit stinging across her cheek.

Kira landed in a crouch, heart slamming. Her bad arm throbbed from the jar. She wiped her palm on her thigh and tightened her grip on the daggers.

“Good,” she breathed. “Stay angry.”

Angry men made bad shots. Angry men leaned out. Angry men forgot there was more than one way to die in a ravine.

She moved again, this time angling toward a shallow fold in the ground where shadows had gathered thick enough to hide a body for a few heartbeats. The scree shifted under her boots. She kept her steps uneven, never letting them settle into a rhythm. Every few strides she slapped one dagger flat against stone or dragged the point through a patch of loose gravel. Noise. Sparks. Movement. Always something to look at.

Above her, the east ridge was changing.

The two near the split boulder were edging farther south, trying to keep both her and the western push in view. The southern pair were no longer calm. One was crouched low behind the cut, bow half-lifted. The other had risen enough to show his shoulders, head turning toward the far side of the ravine.

Kira’s stomach tightened.

That one was about to loose.

She had no clean shot. No angle. No way to reach him. All she had was the same ugly trick, again and again, until it stopped working.

She grabbed a fistful of dirt and small pebbles and hurled it against the cliff face beside her. The sound was weak compared to stone, but she followed it by kicking a loose plate of shale hard enough to send it skidding down the slope with a hollow clatter. Then she raked both daggers across the rock in crossed strokes, sparks flying in wild little arcs.

“Here!” she roared. “Look here, you half-blind bastards!”

The archer hesitated.

It was not much. A breath. A twitch of the bow. His head turned toward her noise. The shot spoiled. The arrow snapped loose and struck the ravine wall far too high, vanishing into the gloom with a faint crack.

Kira bared her teeth.

“That’s it,” she snarled. “Look at me.”

Her lungs burned. Her arm stung. Dust coated the back of her throat until every breath felt like swallowing ground stone. She could hear the western side of the fight shifting—boots scraping, shields grinding, voices strained and ragged. The vanguard was trying to form. Trying to move. Trying to punch through before the archers above found their rhythm again.

Kira could not see the shape of it clearly. She did not need to. She knew what a push like that cost. She knew how fast it died if the high ground got calm.

So she kept moving.

She darted from the shallow fold to a broken shelf of rock, then dropped low and crawled two strides before coming up again behind a slab. An arrow thudded into the stone above her. Another struck the dirt so close her boot shifted.

“Still not dead!” she shouted, and hated how thin her voice sounded. “Come on, then! Make it interesting!”

One of the archers near the split boulder finally lost patience. He rose too far, bow coming up in a hard, impatient draw. Kira saw the line of his shoulders and threw herself sideways without thinking.

The arrow grazed her ribs.

Not deep. Not clean. It tore cloth and dragged a hot stripe across her side before snapping away into the ravine. Kira hit the ground hard, rolled, and came up with a curse stuck in her teeth.

“Fucking hell!” she spat, one hand pressing briefly against her side. Blood slicked her fingers. Not enough to slow her. Enough to piss her off.

She forced herself upright and ran before the next shot could come.

The pain sharpened her. It made the world smaller and simpler. Stone. Cover. Breath. Daggers. The next place to be seen. The next noise to make.

She reached the dead scrub again and kicked it until the roots tore free, then hurled the whole tangled mess toward the base of the ridge. It bounced and skittered, looking bigger than it was in the dim light. At the same time she slashed one dagger across a slab beside her, sending another burst of sparks into the air.

“Over here!” she shouted. “Still here! Still bleeding, you bastards!”

The east ridge answered with another ragged volley.

One arrow struck the dead scrub and shook it. Another punched into the slope beside her knee. The third hit nothing at all.

Kira dropped behind the broken shelf again and pressed her back to the stone. Her chest heaved. Blood from her side made her tunic cling. Her fingers were gritty and slick. She wiped them on her belt and checked her daggers without thinking.

Still sharp. Still in her hands.

She listened.

The southern archers were moving again. Not settling. Not calm. One was cursing now. Another shouted something short and ugly to the pair near the split boulder. Their attention was being pulled in too many directions. That was the point. That was the whole ugly job.

Kira risked another look up.

The archer who had been hunting west had lowered his bow a fraction, head turned toward the noise below. The other was still watching her. The two by the split boulder were arguing with their shoulders, one pointing south, the other pointing down at her.

Good.

Let them argue. Let them waste breath. Let them spend arrows on a woman with no shield, no bow, and nothing but two daggers and a mouth full of curses.

She shifted her weight, ready to move again. Her side screamed. Her arm throbbed. Her boots were loose with grit and sweat.

“Don’t let them settle,” she whispered to herself, because there was no one near enough to hear. “Keep them stupid.”

Then she rose from cover once more, made herself loud, made herself visible, and ran straight into the teeth of the east ridge’s anger.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: The vanguard was struggling, but Kira's constant harassment of the eastern archers was buying us time. "Harder!" I roared, pushing my polearm against the shields of my men, urging them forward. "Don't let them breathe!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira heard the order bounce off the ravine walls and used it like a boot in her spine.

“Then don’t stop!” she shouted back, though the words were mostly swallowed by stone and distance.

She shoved away from the broken shelf and moved along the base of the east ridge, staying bent low. Her side burned where the arrow had grazed her. The torn sleeve clung to her arm with dried blood and grit. She ignored both. Pain could wait until the arrows stopped.

The archers above her were wavering between two fears.

That was the only reason she was still alive.

The two near the split boulder kept glancing south, where the western push was grinding toward the cut. The southern pair were no longer calm either. One crouched low behind the rock lip, bow angled down. The other had risen enough to show his shoulders, head turned toward the far side of the ravine.

Kira saw the danger before it happened.

The standing archer shifted his weight. His bow came up. Not toward her.

“West flank!” Kira roared. “Bow’s turning!”

She had no time for cleverness. She snatched a stone from the dirt and hurled it at the nearest slab. It struck hard, cracking loud enough to jump echoes. At the same time she dragged both daggers across the rock in crossed strokes, sending sparks scattering into the dimness.

The archer flinched.

His shot went high, snapping against the ravine wall somewhere above the fight.

Kira bared her teeth.

“That’s it,” she hissed. “Waste it.”

She broke into another uneven sprint, boots sliding over scree. An arrow punched into the ground a stride behind her. Another hissed past close enough to tug at her belt. She twisted toward a shallow fold in the earth and dropped into it, shoulder hitting stone hard enough to jar her teeth.

For a heartbeat she stayed there, chest heaving.

Dust coated her tongue. Her pulse hammered in her ears. Somewhere across the ravine, boots scraped, shields knocked, and men breathed hard in the ugly rhythm of a push that had not yet broken.

Kira risked a glance upward.

The southern archers were being pulled apart by their own choices. The one watching her kept his bow half-drawn, uncertain. The other had turned farther west, trying to find a clean line on the advancing pressure below. If he settled, he would have time. Time meant dead men.

Kira spat grit and pushed herself up.

“Hey!” she yelled, rising just enough to be seen. “Over here, you useless shits!”

She kicked a loose plate of shale and sent it skidding down the slope. Then she raked one dagger along the bank beside her, throwing another burst of sparks into the gloom. The noise was harsh, grating, and impossible to ignore.

The watching archer loosed.

The arrow struck the edge of the fold and showered her with dirt. Kira dropped again, cursing through her teeth.

“Good,” she breathed. “Stay angry.”

She crawled along the shallow wash, staying below the sightline until the bank curved toward the base of the ridge. There was a crack in the cliff face there, narrow and ugly, with enough handholds to fool a nervous man. Kira had already tried it once. It was not a real route up. Not for her. Not fast enough.

But it looked like one.

She jammed one dagger into the crack and hauled herself upward, boots scrabbling on loose stone. The movement drew eyes instantly. Two bows snapped toward her from the east ridge.

“Ah, fuck,”

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I see the archer on the western ridge finally go down, struck by a well-aimed polearm.* "One down!" I roar, pressing the advantage. "Keep pushing!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira heard the shout from across the ravine and let it sharpen her.

One western bow had gone quiet. She did not need to see the body to know what that meant. The pressure on the vanguard had just eased by one arrow’s worth, and the men on the west ridge would be feeling the loss already.

“Good,” she snarled through gritted teeth. “Bleed them while they’re stupid.”

She came up from the shallow fold in a hard, uneven sprint, boots slipping on loose scree. Her side burned where the earlier arrow had raked her. Her torn sleeve was stiff with dried blood. She ignored both. The east ridge was still the problem. The east ridge still had bows.

The archers above her were wavering. She could see it in the way they moved: too many glances south, too many half-drawn strings, too much silence between them. They had started the fight calm. They were not calm now.

Kira snatched a stone from the dirt without breaking stride and hurled it at the base of the split boulder. It struck with a sharp crack and sent pebbles bouncing down the slope. At the same time she dragged one dagger across the rock beside her, throwing a bright, angry line of sparks into the gloom.

“Still here!” she shouted. “Look at me, you useless bastards!”

The response came fast.

An arrow punched into the ground a stride to her right. Another snapped past her shoulder close enough to stir the air. Kira twisted low and slid behind a broken slab, her breath coming hard. Stone chips rained down onto her shoulders.

She risked a glance upward.

The two archers near the split boulder had stopped arguing. That was bad. They were choosing something. One kept his bow angled down toward her. The other had turned his body south, trying to find a line on the push toward the cut.

Kira’s stomach tightened.

“Cap!” she called, voice raw from dust and shouting. “Two at the boulder! One’s hunting the cut!”

She did not wait to hear if the warning carried. There was no time. The south-facing archer began to settle, knees bending, bow lifting into a cleaner line. If he got that shot off, the wedge would eat it.

Kira broke from cover.

She did not think about it. Thinking would have left her behind the slab. Instead she ran straight at the nearest slab of fallen cliff face, kicked off a loose chunk of rock, and hauled herself up far enough to be seen. One dagger went into a crack in the stone. The other flashed up as she scraped it hard across the rock face.

Sparks burst upward. Metal screamed.

“Hey!” she roared. “Eyes on me!”

The archer flinched.

His release went wide. The arrow snapped into the ravine wall with a harsh crack and vanished into the shadows. Kira dropped back down before the next shot could come, boots skidding on scree. Her bad arm protested. Her side flared hot. She bit back a curse and rolled behind the slab again.

“Fuck,” she breathed, pressing her forehead briefly against the stone. “Stay stupid. Stay stupid.”

The ridge answered with shouted voices. Not calm orders. Angry ones.

One archer swore loudly. Another snapped something short and hard. Boots scraped along the lip above her. They were moving again. Not retreating. Shifting. Trying to decide whether the noisy woman below or the advancing shields on the far side were the greater threat.

Kira wiped grit from her mouth and checked her daggers. Her fingers were slick with sweat and blood, but her grip held.

She could hear the western fight grinding closer to the cut. Shields knocking. Boots slipping. Men breathing hard. The vanguard had not broken. That was enough. That had to be enough.

She peeked around the edge of the slab.

The archer watching her had crouched lower, bow ready. The other was still turned south, trying to find a clean shot at the wedge. Farther along the ridge, one of the southern pair had vanished behind the cut. The other was rising slowly, silhouette tightening against the pale sky.

Kira’s jaw set.

If the one behind the cut settled, he would have time. Time meant aim. Aim meant dead men.

She snatched two stones from the dirt. The first she hurled high toward the split boulder. It struck the ledge above the archers and bounced away with a hollow echo. The second she threw low, hard against a slab closer to her own position. The crack was sharp, immediate, ugly.

Then she raked both daggers across the rock in crossed strokes, sending sparks jumping in wild arcs.

“Here!” she shouted. “Still not dead!”

The archer facing south jerked at the noise. His bow shifted. Not enough. Not fully. But enough to spoil his patience.

Kira saw her chance.

She lunged from the slab and ran toward the dead scrub, staying low. The roots had already been half-torn from the ground. She kicked the remains hard, sending dirt and broken wood skidding down the slope, then dropped to one knee and slapped her dagger flat against the stone.

The sound rang out like a challenge.

The watching archer loosed.

The arrow struck the scrub just as it tumbled sideways. Feathers burst apart. The shaft snapped and spun away. Kira was already moving, throwing herself into the shallow wash with a grunt as another arrow hissed past overhead.

She hit the bank hard and lay there for half a breath, heart hammering.

Dust filled her mouth. Her side throbbed. Her arm felt hot and tight. Somewhere above, a bow creaked.

“Come on,” she whispered. “Come down and do it properly.”

No one took the offer.

Kira forced herself up into a crouch and looked toward the southern end of the ridge. The archer behind the cut had not disappeared. He was low, but not gone. His shadow moved against the stone. He was trying to crawl into position without showing himself.

That was worse than a standing shot. A crawling archer could wait. Could choose. Could put an arrow into the side of the wedge when it least expected it.

Kira’s eyes narrowed.

She could not reach him. Not from the ravine floor. Not without climbing into the teeth of the ridge and getting herself killed. But she could make him think about her instead.

She grabbed a fistful of loose gravel and hurled it against the cliff face. It made a weak, scattering sound. Not enough. She followed it by jamming one dagger into a crack and scraping the other hard across the stone in a long, shrieking drag.

“South cut!” she shouted toward the far side. “One’s crawling low! Don’t let him settle!”

Then she rose just enough to be seen and slapped her thigh with the flat of her blade.

“Over here, you coward!” she roared. “I’m the one making noise!”

The movement drew eyes.

Two arrows snapped toward her at once.

One struck the bank above her head, showering her with dirt. The other hit the edge of the wash so close that the impact kicked grit into her face. Kira flinched, twisted, and went down hard on one knee. Her bad hand slipped. Pain lanced up her arm.

“

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I see Kira go down and a cold dread washes over me.* "Kira!" I roar, my voice raw. "Push! For Kira!" My polearm sweeps, knocking aside an archer's bow. We're almost there.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira’s knee hit the gravel hard enough to jar her whole leg, and for one ugly heartbeat the ravine tilted sideways.

The shout reached her through the broken echo of stone—raw, furious, carrying her name like a curse and a prayer at the same time.

Her teeth bared before she could stop it.

“Not yet,” she hissed through gritted teeth. “Not yet, you loud bastards.”

She forced her weight onto her good leg and came up from the wash in a crouch, one hand pressed briefly to her side. Blood made her fingers slick. The graze along her ribs burned like a brand, and her torn sleeve clung to her arm in a stiff, dirty mess. None of it mattered. Not yet. Not while bows were still moving above her.

The east ridge had gone dangerous in a new way.

The archers were no longer just angry. They were frightened, and frightened men did stupid things. One of the shapes near the split boulder had risen too high, bow jerking as he tried to decide between her and the western fight. The other had crouched lower, nocking fast, shoulders tight. Farther south, the shadow behind the cut was still moving. Still crawling. Still trying to settle into a clean line where he could put an arrow into the flank of the push without earning one back.

Kira saw the glint of his arrowhead against stone and her stomach dropped.

“South cut!” she roared, voice tearing. “He’s drawing! Low and crawling!”

No time to wait. No time to be clever.

She snatched a stone from the dirt—too big, rough-edged, awkward—and hurled it with everything her wounded body had left. It struck the rock face near the cut with a sharp crack, sending chips skipping across the ledge. At the same moment she raked both daggers across the slab beside her in crossed, shrieking strokes. Sparks burst up in wild orange arcs, brief and bright against the ravine gloom.

“Eyes here!” she shouted. “Look at me, you spineless shits!”

The crawling archer flinched.

His shot snapped loose too soon. The arrow hissed across the ravine and struck high on the far wall with a dull, useless crack. Kira let out a harsh breath that might have been a laugh if it hadn’t hurt so much.

“That’s it,” she snarled. “Waste them.”

An answer came from the east ridge immediately: two bows turning back toward her.

Kira moved.

She broke from the wash in a low, uneven sprint, boots skidding over loose stone. The first arrow punched into the dirt behind her. The second snapped past her hip close enough to tug at her belt. She twisted toward the broken shelf she had used before, but her injured side betrayed her as she dropped. Pain flared white-hot along her ribs, and she hit the ground harder than she meant to, shoulder slamming into stone.

“Fuck!” The curse ripped out of her before she could bite it back.

She rolled behind the shelf and lay there for half a breath, chest heaving. Dust coated her tongue. Her pulse hammered so hard it drowned out everything except the fight inside her own skull. Get up. Move. Make noise. If she stayed still, they would settle. If they settled, men on the far side would die.

She did not let herself think about which men.

Kira wiped her bloody palm on her belt and tightened her grip on the daggers. Then she grabbed a loose chunk of rock and hurled it over the shelf without rising. It struck the slope somewhere beyond and broke apart with a satisfying clatter.

“Still here!” she shouted. “Come and earn your pay, you cowards!”

Another arrow thudded into the stone above her. Chips rained down into her hair.

Good. Let them spend arrows on noise.

She risked a glance upward.

The archer near the split boulder who had been facing south had turned back toward her fully now. The other was arguing with him in sharp, panicked gestures. The crawler behind the southern cut had vanished from sight, but his shadow still moved against the rock. He was trying to reposition. Trying to find another angle.

Kira’s jaw tightened.

She could not keep doing this forever. Her body was starting to slow whether she liked it or not. Every breath dragged. Her bad arm trembled when she put weight on it. The blood from her side was not enough to kill her, but it was enough to make her weaker with every sprint.

So she needed to make the ridge break first.

Her eyes swept the base of the cliff. Loose shale. Broken slabs. The narrow crack she had used before, the one that looked like a route up if a man was already afraid. Above it, a chunk of cliff face hung loose in its bed, cracked and weathered, held more by friction than by any kindness of the stone.

Kira stared at it for one heartbeat.

Then she cursed again, because she already knew what she was going to do.

She surged up from cover and ran straight for the crack.

The response was instant.

A bow twanged. An arrow struck the ground a stride to her left. Another snapped past her shoulder so close it felt like a cold blade against her skin. Kira hunched lower and kept running, boots slipping, breath burning. She reached the crack and jammed one dagger into it without slowing, hauling herself upward with a grunt. Pain ripped through her side. Her vision whitened at the edges.

“Ah, fuck,” she gasped, but she did not stop.

She climbed two strides, three, boots scrabbling on loose stone. Then she twisted her body enough to be seen, lifted the other dagger, and scraped it hard across the rock face. Sparks burst upward. Metal screamed against stone.

“Up here!” she roared. “You want me? Come and take me!”

The ridge erupted.

Three arrows struck near her at once. One buried itself in the dirt beside her boot. Another cracked against the cliff face and sent stone chips biting into her cheek. The third snapped past her hand so close her fingers jerked back on instinct.

Kira did not climb higher. She did not need to.

She kicked the loose shale beneath her boot hard, then drove her dagger into the cracked edge of the weathered slab above the climb. The stone shifted. Not much. Enough.

A chunk of rock the size of a man’s fist broke free and tumbled down the slope, striking the ledge below with a heavy crack. Another followed, smaller but faster, bouncing wildly. Dust puffed up from the impact.

One of the archers near the split boulder jerked backward, bow falling from his hands as he scrambled away from the falling stone. The other shouted something and ducked low, covering his head.

Kira dropped before they could recover.

She hit the ground hard, rolled, and came up behind a slab with a curse stuck in her throat. Her side screamed. Her arm felt like fire. For a moment she could not breathe at all, could only kneel there with her forehead pressed against the stone and her bloody fingers wrapped around her daggers.

Above her, the east ridge was in confusion.

She heard it in their voices. Shouting. Overlapping. One man blaming another. The sharp snap of a bowstring loosed in panic, the arrow flying nowhere useful. The sound of boots sliding too fast on rock.

Kira forced air into her lungs. It hurt. She did it anyway.

“South cut,” she muttered, dragging herself upright. “Where are you, you bastard?”

There.

A shadow shifted behind the cut. The crawler had risen slightly, trying to use the confusion to find his shot again. His bow was half-drawn. His head was turned toward the far side of the ravine.

Kira’s blood went cold.

She had no stone big enough. No angle to climb without dying. No way to cross the killzone in time.

All she had was noise.

She lifted one dagger and slammed it flat against the slab beside her. Once. Twice. The sharp cracks echoed up the ravine like hammer blows. Then she scraped the second dagger across the rock in a long, ugly shriek and kicked a loose plate of shale down the slope.

“Hey!” she screamed, putting every scrap of breath and fury into it. “Hey! I’m still here! Look at me!”

The crawler’s head turned.

Just a fraction. Just enough.

His bow wavered.

Kira seized the moment and hurled the last stone she had, not at him, but at the rock face just behind the cut. It struck with a hollow crack and bounced away, echoing twice. The sound made it seem like more movement than one woman could make. Like someone was coming. Like the ridge itself was turning against them.

The crawler flinched fully this time.

His arrow snapped loose and flew high, vanishing into the gloom above the ravine.

Kira laughed, short and ugly, even as pain tightened her face.

“That’s right,” she snarled. “Miss, you useless shit.”

She dropped behind the slab again before the next shot could come. Her body shook now, whether from exertion or blood loss she did not know. She did not want to know. She wiped her daggers on her trousers and checked her grip. Her fingers were trembling, but they held.

The east ridge was breaking.

Not cleanly. Not all at once. But she could hear it. The archers near the split boulder had stopped trying to settle. One was pulling the other back from the lip. The crawler behind the southern cut had gone still, caught between advancing, retreating, and shooting at the woman who would not stay down.

Kira pressed her back against the stone and let herself feel the fight shift around her.

The western side of the ravine was still alive with sound. Boots. Steel. Ragged breathing. The heavy, grinding pressure of men who had not stopped moving. She did not need to see it to know the archers above were running out of time.

She could not give them peace.

Kira rose from cover one more time.

She did not run this time. She stood just enough to be seen, lifted both daggers, and struck them flat against the rock in hard, ringing blows. Sparks flew. The noise echoed up and down the ravine like a challenge.

“Come on!” she shouted, voice raw and ragged. “You’ve still got arrows! Use them on me!”

One archer loosed.

The shaft struck the ground too far to her right. Another came a heartbeat later and snapped past overhead. Neither was close enough to matter.

Kira bared her teeth.

“That all?” she yelled. “Is that all you’ve got?”

No answer came from the ridge. Only more shouting. More scrambling. More fear.

Her knees wanted to buckle. Her side wanted to bleed. Her arm wanted to stop working. She told all of them to shut up.

She slapped her blade against the stone again and moved along the base of the cliff, dragging the other dagger behind her in a bright, scraping line of sparks. Every step hurt. Every breath hurt. She made sure every step made

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I hear Kira's taunts, and the renewed confusion from the eastern ridge. It's working.* "Push through! We're almost there!" I bellow, seeing the western archers falter. My polearm connects with another, sending him sprawling.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The first arrow hit the rocks three feet from Kira's head.

"Contact!" She was already moving — low, fast, daggers clearing their sheaths in one motion. The ravine walls climbed thirty feet on either side. Perfect killzone. The ambushers had the high ground and they knew it.

Another arrow. This one close enough to hear it split the air.

"Cap, I count six on the east ridge, maybe more on the west. We're boxed." She pressed her back against a boulder. Eyes up. Breathing controlled. Waiting for orders.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Kira, east ridge — draw their fire. I'll push west with the vanguard."

I raise my polearm and signal the advance.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The order cut through the ravine sharp and clear. Kira didn't waste breath on a reply. She sucked in one controlled breath, then broke from the boulder.

Gravel skittered under her boots as she ran east, low and fast, her daggers gripped tight. She wanted to be seen. She wanted every bow on that ridge pointing at her.

An arrow slammed into the dirt at her heel. Another whispered past her ear and shattered on stone.

"Shit!" Kira snapped, throwing herself behind a slab of rock. Six heads lined the eastern rim, bows bent, tracking her. A seventh shifted behind a stunted pine, just a glimpse of shoulder.

She leaned out, waving a blade so the steel caught the light. "Oi! You cross-eyed shits! East ridge! Come get it!" Another arrow clipped the rock by her temple, spraying grit.

She ducked back, chest heaving, and shouted over the ringing in her ears. "Cap! Six on the east—maybe seven now! They're taking the bait, but they've got the sun at their backs and the whole fucking high ground. If they pivot, they'll do it faster than we can climb!"

Boots scraped above. A bowman leaned too far over the edge to keep her in his sights. Kira's eyes tracked him, calculating distance and angle.

"That one's leaning too far," she muttered, more to herself than anyone. She didn't throw—not while she needed both blades—but she filed the opening away. "You want a shot, he's hanging his guts over the edge. Otherwise I keep dancing."

Another volley hissed down. Kira rolled, came up in a crouch behind a deadfall, and let out a ragged laugh that was mostly adrenaline. "Yeah, that's right. Keep looking east."

She didn't look west. The Captain had his orders and she had hers; watching wouldn't make the rocks any less steep. Another arrow sparked off the stone beside her boot, and Kira bared her teeth.

"Hurry the fuck up," she breathed.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
(OOC: The last post had me giving an order and then just signalling. This time I'll do some action.)

"Vanguard! Push up!" I shout, my voice echoing back from the ravine walls. I heft my polearm, the heavy steel head glinting dully in the weak morning light. I spot a narrow crevice, almost a chimney, that looks like it might offer some cover and a path up the west wall. "With me! Form up on my flank!" I bark at the nearest mercs.

*I scramble for purchase on the loose scree, my boots skidding. Rocks tumble down around me as I begin to climb, polearm held ready.* "Kira, hold them! We're coming!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira heard the Captain's voice from the west, raw and echoing off the ravine walls. Under it came the rasp of boots on scree and the clatter of dislodged stone. She didn't turn her head. Looking wouldn't steady the rocks under their boots, and the Captain had his orders.

"About fucking time," she breathed.

She risked a glance up at the eastern rim. The picture had changed. The seventh bowman was on his feet behind the stunted pine now, arm raised, gesturing west. Two others had already broken from the treeline and were moving along the ridge, boots kicking up dust, their bows coming down to track something beyond her angle of sight. They were pivoting to bring fire onto the western climb.

"Shit." Kira's grip tightened on her daggers until her knuckles ached. "Cap! They're wise to it! Two, maybe three, breaking west along the rim—they'll have a firing line on your climb in seconds! I'll yank their leash!"

She didn't wait for a reply. She sucked in one hard breath and broke from the deadfall, running east, away from the west wall. Gravel sprayed under her boots. She waved both blades overhead, letting the steel catch the weak light.

"Oi! You slack-jawed whoresons! East ridge, you forgetful cunts! Come and get it!" she screamed.

Arrows answered. One slammed into the dirt at her heel. Another whispered past her ear and shattered on stone. Kira threw herself into a slide, boots first, and slammed against a slab of granite. Pain flared along her shoulder where a shaft had torn through her sleeve. She ignored it, rolling up to one knee.

The two moving west faltered, half-turning back toward the sound of her voice. The leaning bowman above was still there, his bow cranking down toward her. Kira bared her teeth.

"That's right, you beautiful bastards. Keep your eyes east."

Her fingers closed on a fist-sized chunk of loose rock. She wasn't wasting a dagger on a forty-foot throw while six friends waited to come over the edge—but a rock was free. She cocked her arm and hurled it. The stone clanged off the rim a few feet from the leaning bowman, spraying chips. He jerked back with a shout, and for a heartbeat the whole ridge was looking at her again.

"Still on me!" she roared toward the west, eyes locked on the rim. "Keep pushing! They're still looking east!"

Another volley hissed down. Kira ducked, breath sawing in her throat, and pressed herself flat against the granite. She didn't look west. She didn't need to. The Captain had his orders, and she had hers.

"Hurry the fuck up," she breathed.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: An archer targets me directly. I see the draw.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira's head snapped west at the creak of drawn wood.

There—on the western rim—a bowman she hadn't marked before rose from behind a slab of rock. He wasn't looking east. His bow was already at his cheek, the string tight, the steel head of the arrow tracked down toward the scree slope below.

"Cap! West rim!" The warning ripped out of her, raw and sharp. "He's got a draw on you!"

She didn't wait to see if he heard. She broke from cover and sprinted west along the base of the ravine, boots slamming into loose gravel. Arrows from the eastern ridge hissed after her; one clipped the air by her ribs, another sparked off stone at her heel. She ignored them. Her whole world narrowed to the western rim.

She saw the archer's arms tense and the bow start to settle. Too far for a rock to do more than annoy—unless she got closer. She ran harder, daggers low, closing the distance along the floor. Twenty yards. Fifteen.

"Hey! You! Over here, you limp-dicked son of a whore!" she screamed, waving one blade until the steel caught the weak light. "Eyes east, you blind bastard! Look at me!"

She snatched up a fist-sized rock without breaking stride and hurled it with everything she had. The stone clanged off the rim a hand's breadth from the archer's head, spraying chips. His head jerked toward her, the bow dipping as his concentration broke. The string snapped.

The arrow shrieked down and buried itself in the loose scree well wide of the slope, spraying grit.

Kira didn't stop. She ran on, chest burning, putting herself between the western rim and the base of the chimney, both blades up, screaming every curse she knew to keep their eyes on her.

"Keep moving!" she roared toward the west, not daring to glance away from the rim. "He's looking at me now! Move your arses!"

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I don't look back, trusting Kira.* "Vanguard! Move! We've got them distracted!" I yell, scrambling up the crevice. My hands are raw, but I don't care. We need to gain the high ground.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira heard the Captain's shout—raw and close—and then the crevice was suddenly loud with the scrape of boots and the clatter of stone. She didn't turn. Turning wouldn't steady the rock under their hands.

Her world narrowed to the western rim.

The bowman was already recovering. He knocked a fresh shaft and leaned out over the edge, bow coming around to bear on the chimney. Kira saw the angle and made her choice.

"Oi! West rim!" she screamed, waving her blade until the steel flashed. "You throw like a gelded ox! Try me, you slack-jawed—"

He glanced down. His eyes widened.

Kira didn't waste the opening. She reversed her grip on one dagger, planted her boots in the scree, and threw with everything she had left in her shoulder. The blade tumbled upward, a blur of steel against the grey rock. It took him high in the bow arm, just under the shoulder. He screamed and convulsed, the loosed arrow shrieking wild to spark off the rim above the crevice and send stone chips pattering down the rock face.

He toppled back behind the slab, out of sight. Dead or writhing, Kira couldn't tell.

"One down on the west rim!" she roared toward the chimney, already moving. "There's more up there—I never got a clean count!"

Movement flashed further along the western rim. A second shape rose to take the fallen bowman's place. And beyond that, the eastern ridge was boiling. Dust plumed along the eastern treeline as the archers abandoned their fixation on her and scrambled west along the rim, bows coming down to track the chimney. They were pivoting to catch the push in a crossfire.

"Shit." The curse tore out of her. "East rim's coming round! They'll have a firing line on the climb in seconds!"

She broke from the boulder and ran west along the base, boots skidding on loose stone, putting herself in the open where both ridges could see her. She waved the single remaining dagger overhead, screaming every filthy name she could dredge up.

Arrows answered. One whispered past her ribs. Another clipped the granite beside her head, spraying grit into her eyes. She ducked, rolled, and came up in a crouch, chest heaving, shoulder burning where the earlier shaft had torn through her sleeve.

She couldn't hold both ridges forever. Not alone. Not with one dagger and a lung full of fire.

"Cap!" she shouted, voice raw, eyes locked on the rims. "I can't dance for both sides much longer! Whatever you're doing up there, do it fast!"

A fresh volley hissed down from the east. Kira threw herself flat behind a slab of rock as arrows shattered against stone all around her, and bared her teeth at the taste of blood and grit.

"Hurry the fuck up," she breathed.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: I'm separated from the group. Kira can see me across the ravine but can't reach me.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira spat blood and grit, wiping her eyes with the back of a bleeding hand. Across the ravine, she caught sight of the Captain—his figure alone on the rock, cut off from the vanguard. The rest of the group were distant shapes up on the west rim, locked in their own scramble, too far to lend a hand. He was on his own, and the rims knew it.

"Shit!" The curse tore from her throat. She couldn't reach him. The floor between them was a scoured killing ground, arrows still hissing down from both sides. Her shoulder burned where the shaft had torn through, and her left hand was empty—her other dagger was still buried in the west rim bastard. One blade left, and a pocketful of rocks.

Movement snapped her head east. The pivoting archers had almost reached their mark; bows were coming down, tracking the chimney, tracking him. Further west, the second bowman on the rim leaned out over the edge, drawing a bead.

"Cap! You're cut off!" she roared, voice raw. "Vanguard's over the rim—they can't cover you and I can't cross this floor! You're a lone mark on that wall!"

She didn't wait for a reply. She broke from the slab, boots skidding on loose stone, and put herself in the open again. She waved the single dagger until the steel flashed, screaming every filthy name she could dredge up.

"Oi! You slack-jawed whoresons! East rim! West rim! Come and get it, you cross-eyed cunts!"

She stooped, snatched a fist-sized rock, and hurled it at the eastern rim where the archers were settling. The stone clanged off the rim a hand's breadth from the lead bowman, spraying chips. He flinched, his shot going wide, the arrow sparking off empty rock.

"Still on me, you beautiful bastards!" Kira screamed, chest heaving. She stayed in the open, a lone, screaming target between the ridges, eyes locked on the rims.

"Cap!" she bellowed toward the ravine, not daring to look away. "I can't hold both sides much longer and I sure as shit can't get to you! Whatever you're gonna do, do it now! What's your call?"

Another volley hissed down. Kira threw herself flat behind the slab as arrows shattered against stone all around her, and bared her teeth at the taste of blood and grit.

"Hurry the fuck up," she breathed.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I glance at the vanguard, then at Kira. She's a whirlwind of fury, holding their attention.* "Dammit, Kira! Hold them a moment longer!" I roar, then scramble *up* the cliff face like a desperate spider. This isn't ideal, but it's the only way to get to the flank of those archers.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira heard the Captain's voice raw and bitten off over the shriek of fletching. She didn't waste breath arguing. The order was clear enough: keep them looking at her. A moment longer.

She rolled from the slab as another volley hissed down. Arrows shattered on the granite where her head had been a heartbeat before. Kira came up in a crouch, one dagger reversed in her fist, the other hand scrabbling in the scree until it closed on a jagged rock.

On the eastern rim, the pivoting archers had almost reached the bend. She saw the lead bowman's shoulders square, his bow coming level—not at her, but angling down the ravine toward the base of the west wall, toward the chimney. Further along the western rim, the replacement bowman leaned out over the slab, elbows locked, drawing a bead along the same broken scree.

"East rim's coming level!" Kira roared, not caring if the words carried over the noise. "They'll have the angle on the chimney in seconds! West rim's got a fresh bastard leaning out with a clear lane!"

She straightened into the open and hurled the rock. It clanged off the rim a hand's breadth from the lead eastern bowman, spraying chips. He flinched; his shaft shrieked wide and sparked off empty stone.

Then Kira ran, boots skidding on loose gravel, angling west along the base until she was directly beneath the western shooter. She waved the single dagger until the steel caught the weak light, screaming every filthy name she could dredge up.

The western bowman's head jerked down. His bow dipped, tracking her instead of the slope above.

Kira snatched another rock from the scree and threw. It sparked off the slab near his temple. He recoiled, loosing a shot that went wild, the arrow burying itself in the dirt well clear of anything that mattered.

"Still on me, you cross-eyed whoresons!" she screamed, chest heaving. Blood ran down her arm from the torn sleeve; her shoulder burned like fire. One dagger left. A pocketful of rocks. Both ridges still looking at her.

For a moment longer, that was enough.

"Whatever you're doing," she rasped toward the west, eyes locked on the rims, "do it fucking fast."

Another arrow whispered past her ribs. Kira threw herself flat behind a slab as the volley shattered against stone, and bared her teeth at the taste of blood and grit.

"Hurry the fuck up," she breathed.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I'm almost there. My fingers find a solid handhold. One more push.* "Kira! I'm on the rim!" I shout, pulling myself over the edge. *I scan for the archers, my polearm ready.* "Vanguard! On me! Flank them!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira was still flat behind the slab, blood and grit in her teeth, when the Captain's voice cut down from above.

His shout came from the rim—raw, close, edged with the rasp of spent breath. He was up. The words barely had time to land before he bellowed for the vanguard to flank them.

The change in the ravine was instant.

On the western rim, the fresh bowman who had been leaning out over the slab whipped around at the sound. His bow, which had been tracking Kira along the base, snapped up toward the rim behind him. Kira didn't need to see the Captain to read it: the archers had a new target, and it wasn't her.

Along the eastern ridge, the pivoting line faltered. Heads that had been tracking her and the chimney jerked upward, bows coming level with the rim instead of the floor. A shaft that had been loosed at Kira hissed wide and buried itself in the scree a foot from her boot, spent and harmless.

Kira didn't waste the opening.

She rolled to her feet, one dagger still gripped tight, the other hand scrabbling in the dirt until it closed on a jagged rock. Her shoulder screamed as she straightened; blood ran slick down her arm, but she was moving.

Ten yards along the western rim, the replacement bowman was drawing on the voice—drawing on the Captain. Kira saw the string tighten, the steel head dip to bear.

"Cap! West rim! Fresh shooter drawing on you!" The warning ripped out of her, raw as any curse.

She didn't wait to see if it landed. She cocked her arm and hurled the rock with everything left in her shoulder. It clanged off the slab a hand's breadth from the bowman's head, spraying stone chips. He flinched, the bow jerked, and the loosed arrow shrieked wild, sparking off empty air above the rim.

Then the fire on her died. Both ridges were looking up, looking west, looking anywhere but at the bloodied woman on the ravine floor.

Kira sucked in a ragged breath and ran.

Boots skidding on loose stone, she angled for the base of the chimney—the same broken crevice the Captain had used. The crossfire that had pinned her flat was gone, redirected at the men on the rim. She slammed her dagger into a crack in the rock to steady herself, then reached for a handhold and started to haul herself up after them.

"About fucking time," she rasped, tasting blood. One dagger, a burning shoulder, and a climb that would tear her hands to ribbons—but the high ground was finally in play, and Kira meant to be there for the kill.

She drove her boot into a narrow ledge, found purchase, and pulled. The rim above boiled with the sounds of the vanguard engaging, but she didn't look up. She kept her eyes on the rock, on the next hold, and on the climb.

"Hurry the fuck up," she muttered, and climbed.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I see Kira start to climb, and a grim smile touches my lips.* "Good to see you, Kira! Hold fast!" I shout, then turn my attention back to the archers. *My polearm sweeps wide, deflecting an arrow that would have found its mark in one of my men.* "Push them back! No quarter!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira heard the Captain's voice from above—raw, edged with the same desperate fire he'd had since the ambush opened. "Hold fast," he'd barked, as if she had any other choice.

She was holding. Her fingers were locked in a crack in the chimney rock, her boots jammed against the opposite wall, every muscle in her burning shoulder screaming as she hauled herself up another foot. The dagger she'd jammed into the stone for purchase came free with a harsh scrape of steel, and she caught herself with her other hand, snarling at the tear of pain in her arm.

"Not my idea of a fucking holiday," she rasped, tasting blood and grit.

Above her, the rim had turned into a brawl. She didn't need to see it to know the shape of it—the vanguard had crested and hit the western archers hard. She heard the clang of steel, the wet grunt of a man going down, the snap of bowstrings, and the Captain's voice cutting through the noise, barking for them to press the attack.

Then an arrow shrieked down past her ear so close it stirred her hair, and slammed into the rock where her hand had been a heartbeat before. The eastern ridge hadn't forgotten her. Another volley hissed after it, seeking the chimney, seeking anything that moved on the wall.

"Shit!" Kira flattened herself against the face, boots scrabbling for purchase as stone chips pattered down. She didn't look up. She couldn't. The climb was all that existed: the next hold, the next breath, the fire in her shoulder.

And then the rim was right there.

She drove her boot into a narrow notch, found a lip of rock, and heaved. Her fingers hooked over the edge, nails tearing, and she threw herself up and over with a ragged curse, rolling onto the western rim in a spray of loose dirt.

The high ground was a slaughterhouse.

Kira came up in a crouch, one dagger gripped tight, chest heaving. Ten yards away, the vanguard had the western archers reeling—bodies in the dust, a bowman crumpled against a slab with a mercenary's blade in his throat. The fight had pushed past her position, leaving the rim behind the press dangerously open.

And that was when she saw him.

A bowman had broken from the scrap, using a slab for cover. He was on one knee, fresh shaft nocked, his bow coming up—not toward the struggling line, but angling down the rim, tracking the Captain's back. The bastard was lining a shot while everyone else was looking the other way.

"Cap! Behind you!" The warning ripped out of her raw throat.

She didn't wait to see if it landed. Her hand closed on a fist-sized chunk of rim rock and she hurled it. The stone clanged off the slab a hand's breadth from the bowman's head, spraying chips. He flinched, his concentration snapping, and the loosed arrow shrieked wild over the rim to clatter harmlessly down the ravine.

But he was already reaching for another shaft.

Kira ran.

Boots pounding on the rim, she closed the five yards in a heartbeat. The bowman heard her at the last instant, started to turn, but she hit him low and hard, driving her shoulder into his ribs and taking them both down in the dirt. He grunted, scrabbling for a knife at his belt, but Kira's dagger was already moving. She reversed her grip and drove the blade up under the rim of his breastplate, into the soft meat beneath the arm.

He shuddered once and went limp.

Kira ripped the blade free, rolled to her feet, and spat blood from her mouth. Her eyes were already scanning for the next threat, and they found it—the slab where the first west-rim bowman had fallen, the one she'd put her other dagger into what felt like a year ago.

She sprinted to it, dropped to a knee beside the corpse. Sure enough, the hilt of her second dagger jutted from the dead man's shoulder, right where she'd buried it. Kira planted a boot on his chest, wrapped her fingers around the hilt, and yanked.

The blade came free with a wet suck, and Kira let out a ragged, feral laugh. "There you are, you beautiful bitch."

Both daggers. Her hands were torn, her shoulder was a line of fire, and the ravine floor below was still a killing ground—but the high ground was theirs now, however briefly.

She turned toward the press, blades up, chest heaving, and locked her eyes on the eastern ridge where dust still plumed along the treeline. The archers over there were already shifting, bows coming down to track the rim again. She saw the angle, calculated the threat, and barked the observation out over the noise of the fight.

"Cap! Eastern ridge is coming round again—they're lining up to enfilade this rim! We hold this crest or we get pinned and picked apart!" She rolled her shoulder, ignoring the tear of pain, and bared her teeth at the oncoming archers. "Say the word and I'll break their line!"

She didn't know where the Captain wanted her, but she was on the rim, she had both blades, and she was ready to follow him into whatever hell came next.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Kira, with me! We'll clear this ridge, then push east!" I shout. *I point my polearm towards the remaining archers on the western rim.* "No prisoners!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Kira heard the order cut through the din, raw and final. No prisoners. Fine by her.

She didn't waste breath on a reply beyond a ragged, "About fucking time." Her fingers were already tight on both hilts, her shoulder a steady burn, and the remaining western archers were right there—three of them, scrambling backward along the rim toward the eastern treeline, boots kicking up dust. One had a bow half-raised, tracking something behind her, but Kira didn't look to see what. The other two were dropping their bows and reaching for sidearms or trying to nock another shaft.

"Western rim's breaking!" she roared, not knowing if the Captain was behind her or already moving, and not looking to check. "Three left—they're running east to link up with the crossfire! Don't let them reach the bend!"

She broke into a sprint, boots pounding on the rim. The bowman heard her and started to pivot, the arrow coming level with her chest. Kira didn't slow. She dropped into a slide at the last instant—shit, that tore at her shoulder—the shaft whispering over her head, and came up inside his guard with both blades rising. One dagger took him in the thigh, the other in the ribs as she twisted and drove him back against the slab. He folded, choking, and Kira ripped the blades free, already turning.

The second was on her, a short sword in hand, slashing wild. Kira let the blow spend itself on the granite beside her head, felt the jar of it, and answered with a backhanded slash that opened his throat. He went down spraying, and she stepped over him without pause.

The third had made it ten yards toward the eastern bend, bow abandoned, a knife in his fist, screaming for the others over the ridge. Kira didn't throw a blade this time; she needed both. She ran him down, hooked a boot behind his ankle, and drove him face-first into the dirt. He fought like a rat, bucking and snarling, but Kira got a knee in the small of his back and her dagger under the rim of his helmet, into the gap at the base of the skull. He shuddered and went still.

Kira spat a curse and straightened, chest heaving, blood slicking her hands. The western rim was clear behind her—bodies in the dust, no one left standing on this side. But the eastern ridge was no longer waiting. Dust plumed along the treeline as the archers over there finished their pivot; bows were coming down, leveling along the rim toward the push. They had the angle, and they knew it.

"Western rim's clear!" she bellowed, not daring to turn and look for him, keeping her eyes on the eastern treeline. "They're lining up to enfilade—we push now or we get pinned on this crest! I'm with you!"

She started east along the rim at a loping run, both blades low and ready, screening the flank of the advance from the eastern archers, watching the dust and the glint of steel for the first shaft to fly. The high ground was theirs, but it wouldn't stay that way for long.

"Hurry the fuck up," she breathed, and ran for the eastern bend.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *I see Kira clear the western rim with brutal efficiency.* "Good work, Kira! Vanguard! With me! We push east, now!" *I take the lead, polearm sweeping, charging towards the remaining archers on the eastern ridge.* "No quarter, remember!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The command to push east rang out over the rim, raw and final. Kira didn't waste breath on a reply—she hadn't planned on taking prisoners anyway. She was already moving, boots pounding along the crest, both daggers low and ready. Behind her the rim shook with the hammer of boots as the mercs advanced, a line of steel and dust surging toward the bend.

She scanned the eastern treeline. Dust plumed along the ridge as the remaining archers finished their pivot; bows came down, leveling along the rim toward the advancing mercs. Kira's grip tightened on her hilts.

"They've got the angle on the line!" she barked, voice rough. "Volley coming—watch the flank!"

The first shafts hissed down, whispering over the crest. One clipped the air by her ribs; another sparked off stone at her heel. Kira didn't look to see where they landed. She had her own target.

Up ahead, where the rim bent toward the eastern ridge, a bowman rose from behind a slab, shaft nocked, bow coming level with the advancing mercs. Kira snatched a chunk of loose rock from the rim and hurled it. The stone clanged off the slab a hand's breadth from his head, spraying chips. He flinched; his shot shrieked wide and buried itself in the scree well short of the running mercs.

Then they were at the bend, and the eastern ridge was right there.

Archers scrambled in the dust—some dropping bows and clawing for swords, others still trying to loose. Kira picked the closest: a bowman with an arrow half-drawn. She hit him shoulder-first, driving him back into the rocks. He fumbled a knife at his belt; Kira didn't give him time. One dagger took him in the throat, the other punched into his ribs as she twisted free. He folded, choking, and she ripped the blades clear.

The second was backing away, a short sword coming up. Kira let the wild slash spend itself on the granite beside her head, felt the jar of it, and answered with a backhanded cut across his sword arm. He screamed and folded; she stepped in and drove a blade up under his breastplate, into the soft meat beneath the arm. He shuddered and went down.

Kira spat blood and grit, chest heaving. The eastern ridge was breaking. A knot of archers was falling back toward the pines, boots kicking up dust, trying to buy room to nock again.

"Cap—eastern ridge is breaking!" she roared, not looking to see if he heard, keeping her eyes on the treeline. "They're falling back into the trees! If they rally in the pines, they'll enfilade this crest all over again. Say the word and I'll take the fight to them!"

She rolled her torn shoulder, ignored the fire in it, and set herself, both blades up, waiting for the order to come.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "Kira! With me!" I shout, not bothering to lower my voice. *I charge towards the treeline, my polearm raised.* "Let's finish this!"

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The order came from behind her, raw and final. Kira didn't waste breath on a reply. She was already moving, boots pounding on the rim, both daggers low, driving toward the treeline where the broken archers had fled.

The pines swallowed the light. Shadows pooled between the trunks, and the air was thick with dust and the smell of crushed needles. Ahead, she glimpsed movement—three, maybe four, archers scrambling into the thicket. One had his bow up, shaft nocked, tracking something past her toward the crest. Another was on one knee, fumbling a dropped sword from the dirt. The rest were just running, boots kicking up duff.

"Cap! They're rallying in the thicket!" Kira roared, not looking back to see if the words carried. "Three, maybe four—one's got a bow up, and if they get set they'll have a clear lane back at the crest!"

Her hand closed on a fist-sized stone half-buried in the needles. She hurled it. The rock clanged off the trunk a hand's breadth from the bowman's head, spraying bark. He flinched; his loosed arrow shrieked wide and buried itself in a pine well clear of the rim.

Then she was on him.

The bowman heard her at the last instant and started to turn, fumbling a knife at his belt. Kira drove her shoulder into his chest and slammed him back against the trunk. One dagger punched into his thigh, the other up under the ribs as she twisted free. He folded, choking, and she ripped the blades clear, already turning.

The second was on her, a short sword slashing wild in the close quarters. Kira let the blow spend itself on the pine beside her head, felt the jar of it vibrate through her teeth, and answered with a backhanded slash that opened his throat. He went down spraying, and she stepped over him without pause.

The last of the knot had broken and run, boots slipping in the duff as he tried to put a tree between them. Kira ran him down, hooked a boot behind his ankle, and drove him face-first into the needles. He fought like a rat, bucking and snarling, but Kira got a knee in the small of his back and her dagger under the rim of his helmet, into the gap at the base of the skull. He shuddered once and went still.

Kira straightened, chest heaving, blood and sweat stinging her eyes. The thicket around her was quiet but for the rasp of her own breath and the fading snarl of the fight out on the rim. Bodies lay in the duff, no one left standing in this stand of pines.

But further east, beyond the next line of trunks, dust still plumed against the grey light. Shapes moved there—two, maybe three—falling back toward the ravine head, and beyond them the ridge narrowed to a saddle that would give anyone who held it a clean drop onto the crest they'd just taken.

"Cap!" she barked, rolling her torn shoulder and ignoring the fire in it. "Thicket's clear! But there's a handful breaking east—they're heading for the saddle at the ravine head! If they dig in there, they'll have the drop on this whole fucking ridge!"

She set herself, both blades up, eyes locked on the dust pluming beyond the trees. Her hands were torn, her shoulder was a line of fire, and the fight wasn't done—but the high ground was still theirs, and Kira meant to keep it.

"Say the word," she rasped, "and I'll take the fight to them."

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: "No, Kira! Hold fast! Let the vanguard deal with them. We've pushed far enough. Regroup!" I bark, gesturing to the mercs to hold their positions. "Form a defensive perimeter! We're exposed here."

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The first arrow hit the rocks three feet from Kira's head.

"Contact!" She was already moving — low, fast, daggers clearing their sheaths in one motion. The ravine walls climbed thirty feet on either side. Perfect killzone. The ambushers had the high ground and they knew it.

Another arrow. This one close enough to hear it split the air.

"Cap, I count six on the east ridge, maybe more on the west. We're boxed." She pressed her back against a boulder. Eyes up. Breathing controlled. Waiting for orders.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
"Kira, east ridge — draw their fire. I'll push west with the vanguard."

I raise my polearm and signal the advance.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
"On it. Making myself real popular."

She broke from the boulder at a dead sprint, hugging the base of the east ridge where the scree ran loose and loud. Arrows loved movement. Fine. She'd give them movement.

The first shaft splintered against stone a hand's width behind her. The second she *heard* — that flat, hungry whistle — and dropped into a slide as it hissed overhead.

"Over here, you bastards!" she screamed up the slope, arms flung wide for one ridiculous second. "Look at me!"

Four archers on the crest, spaced along the lip. The leftmost was the dangerous one — fast, flat shots, no wasted motion. The other three were firing scared, high and wide.

Kira reversed her grip and threw her left dagger. End over end it tumbled up the cliff and bit into the good archer's forearm. He shrieked, dropped his bow, and the whole line's rhythm broke.

That was the point.

She dove behind a fallen slab as three arrows answered her, hammering into the rock like axe blows. One dagger left. Thirty feet of cliff. Lungs burning.

Movement flickered at the edge of her vision — two figures on the west ridge crest, shifting down toward the ravine mouth. Confirmed, then. The second group was real.

"Cap!" she bellowed across the ravine. "West ridge is live — two moving for the ravine mouth! East is four, one down, they're rattled! I'm going up!"

She spat, cursed under her breath, and started climbing.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content:
*Damn it, Kira!* "Hold the line! West flank, with me! We're not letting them flank us!"

I push forward, polearm held ready, eyes scanning the ridge for those two figures.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
Three body-lengths up the scree. Three. She could've tasted it.

"Copy — breaking east!" A curse, sharp and private under her breath. Then louder, over the clatter of her own descent: "Cap, the second I'm off this wall, the east three have the whole floor zeroed! Keep low!"

She pushed off and let the scree take her — a controlled avalanche, boots skidding, shoulders loose, stones roaring past. An arrow snapped off rock a foot from her ear and she rode the slide beyond it.

At the crest, the wounded archer hauled her dagger out of his forearm with a wet, savage yank and hurled it after her in fury. It cartwheeled past, glinting, and vanished downslope into the loose stone.

"That's comin' out of someone's pay!" she snarled, and hit the ravine floor running.

Halfway across, the east line found its nerve again. Behind her, shafts began to tick and crack off the ground — walking their shots toward the vanguard's push. One skipped off stone and opened a hot line across her outer thigh. She stumbled, caught it, kept moving.

"I'm fine! I'm fine—"

West. Focus west.

The two figures had stopped descending. One knelt on a rock shelf overlooking the mouth — and what came off his back wasn't a bow. Brass caught the light. A horn. Long, curved, mouthpiece already rising.

The second knelt beside him, crossbow leveled down the approach lane. Covering him. Anyone who wanted the horn-blower had to cross thirty yards of open, zeroed ground to reach him.

"West mouth!" she bellowed, sprinting low, one blade. "One's got a HORN — he's calling the rest of them! Other one's covering him with a crossbow! I'm on the horn-blower — somebody keep those east arrows off my back!"

She leapfrogged boulder to boulder, counting the crossbowman's rhythm between shots. Twenty yards. Fifteen. One last stretch of naked ground between her and the shelf.

She broke cover.

The horn rose to his lips.

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: An archer targets me directly. I see the draw.

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
The crossbowman's shoulder dropped. Kira jinked left on instinct alone and the bolt flogged past her hip — close enough to pluck at her shirt — and burst against stone in a spray of grit.

Her thigh was a live coal with every stride. Ten yards.

Movement flickered on the east crest — an archer at full draw, angled down into the ravine. Down into the push.

"ARCHER, EAST CREST — CAP, HE'S ON YOU—!"

Then the mouthpiece touched the horn-blower's lips and there was no breath left for warnings.

Kira threw her last dagger on the run.

It turned over twice and took him under the collarbone. The sound that came out of the horn wasn't a call — a wet, warbling half-note that died in the brass as he folded around the instrument and slid down the rock with it still tangled in his arms.

Half a note. Maybe it carried. Maybe the wind ate it.

The crossbowman heard it die. He looked up mid-span — and Kira hit the shelf before he finished. He dropped the crossbow for a hatchet, swung wide and stupid. She went under it, drove a shoulder into his ribs, and pushed. His heels found the shelf's edge and nothing behind it. He went over with a bark of terror, ten feet into the ravine mouth, and landed folded around a boulder. The crossbow came down after him and broke.

Kira stood at the lip, chest heaving, hands empty.

"Oh, you absolute—" She stalked to the horn-blower, braced a boot on his ribs, and wrenched her dagger free. Wiped it on his coat. "Mine."

Then the far horn sounded.

Low. Long. Way out past the west ridge, thinned by distance and stone. One note. Held. Gone.

Kira went very still. "*Shit.*"

"Cap!" Flat, carrying. "West mouth is ours — horn-blower's down, his cover man went off the shelf and isn't walking anywhere. But his half-note got out, and something just answered from further west. That wasn't a reply. That was a *second* horn. There's a bigger party out there."

Across the ravine, the east three were still up, bows tracking the vanguard's advance.

"East still has three, walking fire toward your line. I've got the high shelf and no throw worth making. I can hold here and drop rock on the east archers, or come down and join you. Call it."

dialogue.name: Captain
dialogue.content: *Damn it. More of them.* "Kira, stay on the shelf! Keep those east archers pinned! I'm moving the vanguard to cover. We'll push through the mouth."

dialogue.name: Kira
dialogue.content:
"On it."

She put the order behind her and went to work.

First: loot. Boot to the horn-blower's ribs, roll him, cut his belt free. A knife — ugly cousin to a dagger, but it'd live — and a waterskin. She threaded the knife where her second blade used to sit and made a private note to stop hurling her pay into dead men's chests. The graze on her thigh had soaked her breeches dark; she tore a strip off his sleeve, cinched it high with her teeth, and hissed through the knot. Below the shelf, the crossbowman was a broken tangle around his boulder, moaning, the crossbow in three pieces beside him. She spared him one glance. No time to be merciful or thorough.

Then the real weapon: the shelf itself. Flat stones, edge-heavy, stacked along the lip like the gods owed her a favor. She sighted across the gap — thirty-odd yards, twenty up — spat, and threw.

Her first rock burst on the crest lip a foot from the leftmost archer. Shards sprayed his whole line. He flinched so hard his arrow went into the sky.

"Welcome to the other side, boys!"

An arrow answered — cracked off the shelf edge a hand's width from her knee. "Yeah, yeah. *Fuck* you too." She stayed low between throws, popping up just long enough to heave. Didn't need clean hits. Needed stone shattering close enough to fill their eyes with grit every time they touched a string. One of them leaned out for a careful shot and took her next rock full across the collarbone — he dropped behind the lip and stayed there. Her arm was a banked coal by the tenth stone, and it was worth it. The east fire went ragged: *up, loose, duck.* No more walking shots. No more sightlines.

"Cap!" Flat, carrying across the ravine. "East is pinned — two still shooting, both rattled, can't hold an aim on your push while I'm throwing. Third one's down. But I can see west from up here, and the math's gone bad."

She kept her eyes on the valley spine while she talked. "Twelve, maybe fifteen, skirmish line, hard march. Four minutes at that pace, less if they run. And one just broke ahead of the line — runner, moving fast. Two minutes, maybe less. He'll have eyes on this mouth before his friends do."

She hefted the dead man's horn. Turned it over in her hands.
